title: Strict scalar Hom identification and normalized evaluation square
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $\varphi:R	o S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, $E=S\otimes_R-$ the sheafified ordinary scalar extension and $U$ restriction [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Extend them termwise to unbounded complexes. Use the actual product Hom complex and local evaluation [def-pur-hom-complex] [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. There are natural chain isomorphisms $
u_A:S\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}UEA$ and $	heta_{P,N}:U\mathcal Hom_S^ ullet(EP,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_R^ ullet(P,UN)$, with $
u(s\otimes x)=s\otimes x$ and $	heta(g)(x)=g(1\otimes x)$ on every slice and homogeneous component. For any $R$-complexes $P,J$, any $S$-complex $N$ and chain map $q:EJ	o N$, there is a unique $S$-linear chain map $\sigma_q:E\mathcal Hom_R^ ullet(P,J)	o\mathcal Hom_S^ ullet(EP,N)$ satisfying $\sigma_q(s\otimes f)(t\otimes p)=st\,q(1\otimes f(p))$. Put $\alpha_S(s\otimes f)(p)=s\otimes f(p)$. The strict equality $	heta_{P,N}\,U(\sigma_q)\,
u_{\mathcal Hom(P,J)}=\mathcal Hom_R(P,Uq)\,\mathcal Hom_R(P,
u_J)\,\alpha_S$ holds before localization. All maps commute with maps of the input complexes and compatible changes of coefficient rings and of $q$. No flatness, boundedness or K-injectivity is assumed.

proof.text: For the strict square, evaluate on $s\otimes f$, in degree $n$, coordinate $i$, at $p$. The formulas of [lem-sfb-slice-scalar-hom-chain-adjunction] and [lem-sfb-scalar-hom-chain-evaluation] give $s q(1\otimes f^i(p))$ on the left and $q(s\otimes f^i(p))$ on the right. They agree by $S$-linearity of $q$. Equality of all product coordinates [def-pur-hom-complex], then the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and uniqueness through module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], prove equality of chain maps. The evaluation is precisely product projection followed by evaluation at the identity of the slice [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]; no localization or replacement is involved.

proof.text: For any commuting coefficient square, the maps already supplied satisfy every normalization hypothesis of [lem-sfb-scalar-hom-chain-coefficient-coherence]. Apply its four chain equations to obtain coefficient compatibility of $\nu,\theta,\alpha_S,\sigma_q$, with its normalized iterated-extension identifications and restriction mate. Its arbitrary $w:BN\to N'$ and compatible $q'$ cover semilinear target changes as well as scalar-extended targets, and its identity/composite compatibility covers coefficient towers. Combined with the input naturality in steps 1–2, this gives the last clause. None of the three lemmas requires flatness, boundedness or K-injectivity.
